title: The pencil trick that shows exactly where to sand a glued-up panel flat

slides.title: Is it flat, or does it just look flat?
slides.sub: A pencil tells you the truth

slides.label: The problem
slides.heading: You can't see high spots
slides.body: After a glue-up, boards sit a hair higher or lower than their neighbors. Sand by feel and you dig dips in some places and miss ridges in others.

slides.heading: The trick
items: Scribble light pencil lines across the whole surface.
Sand with a flat block or sander, keep it moving.
Lines gone = flat. Lines left = low spots.
slides.tip: Wear a dust mask and eye protection when sanding.

slides.label: Why it works
slides.heading: High spots lose the lines first
slides.body: The sander only touches the high spots at first, so their pencil disappears first. Keep going until every line is gone, then redo it with each finer grit.
slides.fix: Redraw the lines every time you change grit.
